To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the leaching of NO 3‐N and P can be significantly increased by heavy applications of biosolids and co‐composts; (2) the leaching risk of heavy metals from soils treated at high loading rates is low; and (3) the leguminous covercrop, sunn hemp ( Crotalaria juncea ), significantly increases the leaching of N and P when returned to the soil, but not heavy metals.
at heavy loading rate, biosolids and coal ash can increase the leaching of NO 3‐N, inorganic P and some heavy metals from a calcareous soil.
at heavy loading rate, leaching of N and P from soil amended by biosolids can be a significant concern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential risk of groundwater pollution from heavy metal leaching from soil amendments and cover crops.
the potential risk of groundwater pollution by heavy metals and N and P from soils amended at a heavy loading rate of biosolids (equivalent to a rate of 50 t dry weight ha− 1).
the effects of heavy loading rates of amendments on the leaching of nutrients and heavy metals from a calcareous soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy loading of the biosolid and co‐composted yard waste amendments at 205 g pot −1 did not cause any significant leaching of heavy metals from the calcareous soil.
the heavy loading rates of the amendments tested did not cause any significant increase in leachate concentration of the heavy metals tested.

the application of coal ash and N-viro soil to the calcareous soil at the heavy loading rate of 205 g pot- 1 (50 t ha- 1) would be the safest, followed by the application of biosoloids, co-compost, and yard waste compost, and the incorporation of sunn hemp and sorghum into the soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biosolids application can increase the concentration of NO 3‐N in the leachate significantly.

at the heavy loading rate of 205 g pot −1 (50 t ha−1), biosolids increased the concentration of NO 3‐N and P, and the concentrations of heavy metals (Ca, Fe, Zn and Co) in leachate, while N‐viro, co‐compost, and coal ash decreased the concentration of inorganic P and the concentrations of Ca, Mg and Fe in leachate.
the application of biosolides at a heavy rate (50 t ha−1) can cause the leaching of NO 3-N and P to increase significantly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of biosoloids at a loading rate of 205 g pot − 1 (equivalent to about 50 t ha − 1 of dry weight), can increase the leachate concentration of NO3 − significantly.

biosolids can cause leaching of NO 3‐N at high loading rates, and that the use of leguminous cover crops, sunn hemp in particular, can cause the leaching of NO₃‐N to be increased by about 7 times over non‐legume cover crops.

the heavy metals in the amendments were not leached at levels that would be harmful to humans or the environment, although there was a significant increase in the concentration of Ca and Mg in leachate when biosolids or N‐viro were used as soil amendment.
